name: Baseline Lookout
summary: Federal groundhouse on Baseline Mountain, built in the late 1920s and staffed until the late 1940s; a tower to the west replaced it, and the old building is a hike destination.
design: 3 by 3 m (10 by 10 ft) hip-roof wooden groundhouse on a concrete foundation

access.note: Reached on foot from a dirt access road with poorly signed trails; no closure or permit described in the sources read. The active summit tower is staffed in season, and no source says the public may climb it.

visit.trail_note: Out-and-back hike of about 10.8 km return with about 701 m of climbing, rated hard; most accessible from Rocky Mountain House. The guide describes a small shelter at the top (updated August 2026).

events.note: Register: one of at least three surveyed in the late 1920s, and built by the federal Canadian Forest Service; the register gives no build date. 1928 is a placeholder year for 'late 1920s', not a date any source gives.
Register: the groundhouse was abandoned after the successor tower was completed. Placeholder year as above.
Register: a new 80 ft tower and cabin about half a mile west was completed, and the groundhouse was then abandoned. Placeholder year as above.
Register: staffed by provincial personnel until the late 1940s. 1948 is a placeholder year, not a stated date.

Travel Alberta: the fire tower site was upgraded in the 1990s to a new tower location on the adjacent summit with an access road. 1990 is a placeholder year; this does not match the register's late-1940s dates.
Registered June 5, 1996; nominated by Bob Young, Alberta Land and Forest Service
